text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Dutch central bank DNB increases interest rate on advances by 0.1 pct to three percent. (p1)
- U.S. Acquisitions financial services groups ING and Aegon have created a second large market for their shares on Wall Street (p1)
- Five big advertisers join forces to buy advertising space via Kobalt Media Services. (p1)
- Losses from Nedcar's production of the Volvo 400-series cost the Dutch government some Dfl 300 million. (p3)
- State economic planning bureau CBP maintains higher 1998 tax windfall forecast of around three billion guilders. (p5) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Cabinet opts for a 1750 hectare extension of Rotterdam's port on the Maasvlakte. (p1)
- Rabobank seeks European partners for promoting home- banking in Europe. (p2)
- Cabinet plans to increase fiscal opportunities for small business-owners to build up a pension. (p1)
- Brewer Heineken is making preparations for a temporary closing of its Cambodian brewery. (p25)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM worried about delay in building Schiphol airport's fifth runway. (p1)
- KLM and its U.S. partner Northwest Airlines open scheduled flight to Seattle despite their quarrels. (p7)
- Contaner transhipment company ECT changes its course after agreement with Denmark's Maersk.
